$logging.description: Per-host log root paths (canonical host keys: MacBook, NixOS, Windows).

lifecycle.description: Shared policy data for the service (mount attempt counts, timings, watchdog cadence). Consumed by runners and watchers on every host from a single definition. Contains no failure-classification tokens and no user-facing text: classification is per host (see each host's mount backend) and remedies live in the code that emits them.

mountAttempts.description: Maximum mount attempts in ONE runner invocation before the runner gives up. Governs the mount runner only; it is not a retry count for the service watchdog.

mountRetryBackoffSeconds.description: Seconds to sleep before the NEXT mount attempt, indexed by attempt number (1-based): attempt N sleeps element N-1. CLAMPED, never extrapolated - when `mountAttempts` exceeds the schedule length the LAST declared value is reused, so every delay a runner sleeps is a declared value and no runner may invent one beyond the list. Hosts must not diverge on this rule.

mountAttachTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for the mount to become live after rclone starts. A TIMEOUT, not an interval and not a retry count: when it elapses the attempt is recorded as a failure.

watchdogTickSeconds.description: Seconds the service watchdog sleeps between ticks, on every host. Bounds how long a service can stay down before revival is even attempted. Distinct from watchdogRepairTimeoutSeconds, which bounds ONE repair call rather than the gap between ticks.

watchdogRepairTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds allowed for ONE supervisor repair call before the watchdog abandons it as timed out. Bounds a single call, not the gap between ticks; distinct from watchdogTickSeconds.

network.description: Named network endpoints exposed by this service (omit for services with no network interface, e.g. Unix-socket-only).

hostLogRoots.description: User and system log directory paths for one host. MacBook logDir uses ~/Library/Application Support/nucleus/logs (native USER root) for nucleus/logs consistency across hosts.

logDir.description: User-level log root. May use ~ (POSIX) or %ENV% (Windows) templates.

systemLogDir.description: System-level log root. MacBook uses /Library/Application Support/nucleus/logs (native SYSTEM root).

hostLoggingRoots.description: Log roots keyed by canonical hostname (MacBook, NixOS, Windows).

loggingEntry.description: Logging configuration for a service. Per-platform entry overrides the top-level logging block.

capture.description: Which streams to capture: all, stdout, stderr, or none.

dirs.description: Log subdirectories this service needs under each log root. Values are subdirectory names (may differ from the service key, e.g. 'caddy' uses 'https-proxy'). Multiple dirs are declared when a service has both launchd-captured stdout/stderr and application-level logs on separate paths (e.g. jellyfin uses 'jellyfin' for launchd capture and 'jellyfin-app' for its internal --logdir).

system.description: Subdirs needed under the system-wide log root.

user.description: Subdirs needed under the per-user log root.

instanceDirs.description: Log subdirectories that exist once per runtime instance of a prefixMatch entry, named from an <instance> token. The service itself creates these directories (apply-time dir provisioning cannot know the instance ids), while rotation and expiry walk the whole log root recursively. Declared per platform host entry, not top-level: instance ids differ per host, and a host without file capture (journald) declares none.

system.description: Per-instance subdirs needed under the system-wide log root.

user.description: Per-instance subdirs needed under the per-user log root. The <instance> token expands to the instance id minus the host entry's 'service' prefix.

eventLog.description: Windows Event Log query config for native services (ignored on other platforms).

logName.description: Event Log name to query via Get-WinEvent (default: Application).

provider.description: Event Log provider name registered by the service.

level.description: App-level log severity hint (passed as env var to the service if supported).

maxFiles.description: Number of rotated archives to keep.

maxSize.description: Maximum log file size in bytes before rotation.

sanitize.description: Strip control characters (ANSI escapes, \r) from log output.

launchdDomain.description: Actual launchd domain for this service (gui/<uid> or user/<uid>). Determines the launchctl target. Required when scope=user.

scope.description: Service scope (user agent or system daemon). Determines watchdog filtering and elevation requirements.

justification.description: Why this service is user-scoped when the policy default is system-wide. Required when scope=user.

onDemand.description: Service is intentionally on-demand — the watchdog must not auto-restart it when it is not running. Use for services with KeepAlive=false that are started explicitly by apply/vm/svc.

prefixMatch.description: Match all services with this prefix

runAsUser.description: Service runs as the console user via UserName (not root). Needed for chown logic on macOS.

socketActivated.description: Service is socket-activated by launchd (e.g. sshd). Shows as "listening" in status instead of "inactive".

unitPath.description: Canonical install path for the supervisor unit file. Backend resolves __INSTANCE__ token and leading ~ expansion. Required for file-backed supervisors (macos-launchctl, nixos-systemctl).

onDemand.description: Service is intentionally on-demand — the watchdog must not auto-restart it when it is not running. Use for services with KeepAlive=false that are started explicitly by apply/vm/svc.

prefixMatch.description: Match all services with this prefix

endpoint.description: A single network endpoint with host, port, and protocol.

host.description: IP address or hostname the service binds to or is reachable at.

serviceRuntimeEntry.description: Service runtime configuration for one host

hostEntry.description: Host-specific service configuration with platform reference

prefixMatch.description: Match all tasks with this prefix

service.description: Scheduled-task name prefix for prefixMatch entries. Combined with taskPath it forms the full task id, so instance ids can be derived from the cloud-drive manifest rather than stored.

justification.description: Why this service is user-scoped when the policy default is system-wide. Required when scope=user.

prefixMatch.description: Match all units with this prefix

unitPath.description: Canonical install path for the systemd unit file. Backend resolves __INSTANCE__ token and leading ~ expansion. Required for file-backed supervisors (nixos-systemctl).
